title: One action, two verbs: aspect
description: Choose between the imperfective verb (process, habit) and the perfective one (a finished result).

blocks.text: Most Polish verbs come in pairs. The imperfective verb describes an action as a process, something repeated or a habit: czytać, pisać, robić. The perfective verb describes one completed action with a result: przeczytać, napisać, zrobić. The perfective verb is often the imperfective one with a prefix. In the past both are common; in the present only the imperfective is possible, because a perfective verb in the present form refers to the future.

blocks.translation: I read the newspaper every day.
Yesterday I read the whole book.
I was writing a letter all evening.
I wrote the letter and sent it.
Tomorrow I will do the shopping.
blocks.note: A perfective verb in the present form means the future.

lines.speaker: Kuba
lines.translation: Not yet. I am doing it now.

lines.speaker: Kuba
lines.translation: I will finish in half an hour.
